Description - GET /File.aspx

Plain GET of the signed URL. The client resumes and splits downloads with Range: bytes=N-M / bytes=N- and parses Content-Range: bytes N-M/T; the default config allows one connection per file (max-connection-count = 1). An expired link triggers RefreshFileUrl. The URL is reusable (several GETs worked). Headers: the downloader's GET carries Range when resuming or splitting, plus the Qt 4.8.5 defaults User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0, Accept-Encoding: gzip, Accept-Language: <locale>,en,* and Connection: Keep-Alive (Inferred for this request).

Player streaming: the player GETs the player.audio URL with Icy-MetaData: 1, Accept-Encoding: (a single space, disabling Qt's gzip) and optionally Range: bytes=N-; it requires HTTP 2xx, Content-Length > 0 and no x-nofile header, and treats a redirect to /File.aspx as failure.

Path notes

The signed URL returned by Download (FileEntry/url) and RefreshFileUrl (url): http://sNNNN.chomikuj.pl/File.aspx?e=…&pv=…. The client never builds it; it uses the URL verbatim.

Client vs live - discrepancies

None recorded for this operation. The document-wide register is on the API overview.

Security notes - findings that concern GET /File.aspx

  • C-01 High All client traffic uses plain HTTP (SOAP, upload, resume check, downloads, web login hand-off, updater, crash reports). The SOAP service also answers on HTTPS, but the client never uses it.
  • S-08 Low Signed File.aspx?e=…&pv=… download URLs are reusable bearer URLs (repeat GET and Range work); expire was always empty, so their lifetime is unknown.

From x-security-notes in the spec. Ratings and scope are explained on Security & privacy.
